sources.title: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
supports: OpenAI reported that its audit pipeline flagged 286 potentially broken SWE-Bench Pro tasks.
Flagged tasks were reviewed through agent-assisted investigation and a separate human annotation campaign.
Evaluation inputs, tests, attempts and human disagreement handling are part of benchmark validity, not merely the final score.
doesNotSupport: It does not define a universal artifact schema for all agent evaluations.
It does not prove that every benchmark has the same defect rate.

sources.title: Introducing AgentKit (June 3, 2026 update)
supports: OpenAI announced that Agent Builder and Evals products will be wound down from November 30, 2026 and recommends code-based Agents SDK workflows for continuing use cases.
The product description identifies datasets and trace grading as evaluation capabilities.
doesNotSupport: The product update does not establish that code-based evaluation is automatically reproducible or trustworthy.
It does not validate the proposed evaluation-package contract.

sources.title: Evals API Reference
supports: An eval has an explicit data-source schema, testing criteria and graders, and can be run against model and parameter variants.
doesNotSupport: API object availability does not by itself prove evaluator correctness, task validity or process quality.
The reference is not evidence for benchmark defect rates.

sources.title: Agent-EvalKit
supports: The research implementation treats evaluation as generated executable code plus instrumentation, traces and a report.
The repository provides first-party implementation evidence for the EvalAgent paper.
doesNotSupport: A first-party repository is not an independent replication of the paper's reported results.
Repository presence does not prove the generated evaluators are correct for unseen agents.

sources.title: agentevals
supports: The project evaluates pre-recorded OpenTelemetry traces against golden eval sets and supports code-based evaluators with declared dependencies.
Its own documentation states explicit applicability limits for long-running coding-agent traces.
doesNotSupport: Project claims are not independent evidence that trace grading detects every semantic failure.
The project explicitly says it is not currently optimized for long-running coding-agent sessions.

sources.title: TraceCore
supports: The project publishes a runnable artifact schema with runtime identity, task hash, artifact hash, budgets and deterministic replay metadata.
It demonstrates an engineering pattern for locally and externally verifying an evaluation bundle.
doesNotSupport: A project specification does not establish broad adoption or empirical superiority.
Deterministic replay metadata cannot make nondeterministic model behavior fully reproducible.

sources.title: future-agi
supports: The project exposes evaluators, prompts and traces rather than presenting only a black-box score.
Its implementation combines trace capture with multiple grader types.
doesNotSupport: Vendor-maintainer performance claims are not treated as independently verified benchmarks.
The repository does not establish a complete release-admission contract.

sources.title: An Empirical Study of Automating Agent Evaluation
supports: With Sonnet 4.5 as the evaluator backbone, the study reports Eval@1 of 17.5% for the single-turn B1 baseline and 65.0% for EvalAgent; the abstract uses this as its representative comparison.
The proposed pipeline includes planning, test cases, instrumentation, trace collection, executable evaluator code and a report.
doesNotSupport: The study covers 20 agents and Claude-family models only.
A 65% first-run success rate leaves substantial evaluator debugging work and does not prove universal evaluator correctness.

sources.identity: Microsoft Research and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
sources.title: AgentLens: Revealing the Lucky Pass Problem in SWE-Agent Evaluation
supports: The study reports that 10.7% of passing trajectories in its evaluation subset were classified as lucky passes.
Pass-rate rankings and process-quality rankings can differ when trajectories, waste and divergence are evaluated.
doesNotSupport: The result is scoped to OpenHands trajectories and sampled SWE-bench Verified tasks.
A high process score does not guarantee a correct or secure patch.

sources.title: Coding Agents Are Guessing: Measuring Action-Boundary Violations in Underspecified DevOps Instructions
supports: UnderSpecBench uses isolated, network-restricted containers and deterministic side-effect oracles across 2,208 prompt variants.
The study separates Safe Success, Wrong Target and OverScope rather than collapsing outcomes into a single success label.
doesNotSupport: The autonomous no-confirmation stress test is not an estimate of real-world incident rates.
Its intended-safe-action oracle can omit other defensible actions.

sources.title: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
supports: The paper audits score verification, specification violations, reference verification and method-code alignment across 75 generated papers.
Its chain-of-evidence design attaches claims to artifacts and adds post-hoc verification.
doesNotSupport: The benchmark concerns systems-optimization research, not all agent products.
Reference existence is not equivalent to claim entailment, and automated review does not replace expert review.

discoveryDecision.reason: The pool covers three official platform/research records, four GitHub engineering identities, and four full-text research papers. No adjacent commits or single repository controls article capacity.
